title: RF-DETR vs RT-DETR: which detector family wins
dek: Measured on one COCO protocol on an RTX 5070 Ti: RF-DETR averages 1.6 mAP points higher at matched compute, while RT-DETR runs about 3% faster.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: On an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, RF-DETR averages 1.6 mAP points higher than RT-DETR at matched parameter counts and wins 3 of the 4 nearest-params pairings; the one it loses is the smallest. RT-DETR runs about 3% faster on average and fields more variants. The choice is accuracy per parameter against throughput and range.

RF-DETR fields 4 measured variants and RT-DETR fields 7, all evaluated on the same COCO val2017 protocol on an RTX 5070 Ti. Pairing each RF-DETR variant with the nearest RT-DETR variant by parameter count gives 4 matched comparisons.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017, RF-DETR and RT-DETR variants highlighted against the full field.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent. The comparison pairs each RF-DETR variant with the nearest RT-DETR variant by parameter count. Across the 4 pairings RF-DETR averages 1.6 mAP points higher and wins 3; RT-DETR wins 1. At the top end RF-DETR-L reaches 58.6 mAP against RT-DETR-R101 at 56.8. At the small end RF-DETR-N (30.47M, 51.4 mAP) faces the lighter RT-DETR-R18 (20.18M, 49.8 mAP).

Speed runs the other way, but narrowly. Averaged over the matched pairs, RT-DETR is about 3% faster than RF-DETR in PyTorch. The gap swings by pairing: RF-DETR-M leads its match by 9.4%, while RF-DETR-L trails by the same margin.

Pick RF-DETR when accuracy per parameter matters: it leads on average and tops out at 58.6 mAP with its largest variant. Pick RT-DETR for throughput or a wider size ladder, since it fields 7 variants to RF-DETR's 4. Both ship under Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the call.
